title: HEAT Sentinel reticle manifest
description: One `reticle.json`, in one folder under `reticles/`. Describes a single shipped sight: what it is, who made it, which file holds the drawing, and where the author thinks it should sit. Everything except `id`, `name` and `file` has a working default, because a reticle that only names its file is a legitimate contribution.

v.description: Manifest version. 1 is the only one there has been.

id.description: Stable address of this reticle, and the folder name. Lower-case, digits, dash. It travels in settings and in links, so renaming one is a breaking change for anybody who applied it.

name.description: What a person calls it, shown in the tray.

file.description: The drawing, relative to this manifest's own folder. No `..`, no absolute paths, no subdirectories above this one.

kind.description: What `file` is. Omitted, it is inferred from the extension and then from the bytes, exactly as an import from disk is. `svg` is flattened to vector shapes on import, not handed to the game as a document.

author.description: Who drew it. A name or a handle; not an email.

license.description: SPDX identifier, or a short phrase for anything without one. Required in practice by the contribution rules even though the schema does not force it, because a drawing with no stated licence cannot be shipped.

source.description: Where it came from, for credit and for checking updates: a forum post, a repository, a gallery page.

description.description: One or two sentences on what it is for. Shown under the name.

preview.description: A small picture of the sight in use, relative to this folder. Not the drawing itself.

unitRef.description: What a coordinate of 1.0 means for a `.blk`. `height` is right for everything measured so far; the field exists because one screenshot is one aspect ratio. Ignored for a picture.

opts.description: The placement the author recommends. Applied WITH the reticle, so a drawing made for another game's proportions arrives fitted rather than needing four sliders moved. Every field is optional and clamped by `cdp/sight.py` on the way in.

offset.description: Screen pixels at 1080p, added after scaling.

color_main.description: Overrides whatever the drawing asked for. Leave it out unless the reticle only reads in one colour.

spread_scale.description: Multiplies everything in a pack that follows the gun's spread. 1 is the game's own circle, 0.75 the smallest allowed.

image.description: Placement for a picture reticle. `anchor` is the point of the BITMAP that aims, as a fraction of it, and it is the one field a picture cannot be used well without.

p.description: Where that anchor point sits, relative to the aim point, in sight units.

w.description: Width in sight units. 0 means the bitmap's own pixels.

h.description: Height in sight units. 0 keeps the bitmap's aspect ratio, which is almost always what is wanted.

mil.description: Treat `p`, `w` and `h` as milliradians rather than screen fractions. Needs the user's FOV calibration to mean anything.
